concerns.message: The plan names two ways out, an expiry (`expireReservation`) and a consented leave (`quitPlayer`). A third path is left out. When a fighter drops, the room calls `allowReconnection(client, DUEL_RECONNECT_SECONDS)` (MatchRoom.ts:213). When that runs out, Colyseus calls `onLeave` with the leave not consented, about 10 s after the drop. The duel forfeit hangs on that same `onLeave` → `machine.leave` (duelMachine.ts:233-241). At that point `expireReservation` refuses: players.ts:150-151 returns `not-disconnected` or `reservation-active` because the ledger deadline is 1200 ticks. A related problem: a world drop's 60 s reservation runs on Colyseus' wall clock, while the ledger deadline counts world ticks. If the fixed timestep falls behind, Colyseus can fire first and `expireReservation` is refused the same way. A request carrying the future deadline tick is not a fix: it would make every later request stale.
concerns.consequence: Suppose a worker writes `onLeave(consented ? quit : expire)`. The ship is removed, but the ledger keeps the player as connected or disconnected. The duel settlement then hands the loser's remaining rubbings back to that player, who has no ship, and no cache is ever made. checkLedger still passes, because the player is still in the match. No acceptance test covers a drop in the middle of a duel. So rubbings silently leave the 8-rubbing race, which breaks §4, §12 and §19 ('cannot erase rubbings'). Settle the mapping first. Option (a): any leave that is not an expiry of the ledger deadline is a `quitPlayer`, and the cache goes at the nearest dock. Option (b): per §12, a fighter keeps the 60 s seat, the 10 s duel forfeit runs on its own world-tick timer, and the player respawns. In both cases, expiry should come from `reservationDeadline` in `advance()`, with Colyseus' window only as an outer bound. Add an integration test for a drop mid-duel.

concerns.message: Sources are dealt at random from the room's randomness. In the slice (4 islands × 2 sources, 4 sun and 4 moon), 16 of the 70 equally likely moon layouts put one moon on every island. In those layouts, a player at any island collects sun first, because `startCollect` goes in type order. `theft-loop` needs the two players to collect different types at different islands, so it cannot pass in about 23% of matches. The e2e server runs in its own process, so the test cannot read the ledger. It can only see an island's types by mooring there.
concerns.consequence: The browser check fails about 1 time in 4.3. A worker may get lucky locally and the verifier then fails. Add a test-only assignment or seed setting that is off by default, like PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_PLACEMENT, and never derive it from the match code. Integration tests should read the room's ledger to choose islands.

concerns.message: Caches are always placed at island docks: the respawn dock, or the nearest dock by sea. An island dock is also where that island's sources are collected with the same E hold. The plan does not say which one E targets when a sealed eligible source and a cached eligible rubbing are both there. It also does not cover two caches at one dock. Separately, 'keep holding' chains on its own: after one collection, a held E starts the island's next eligible source.
concerns.consequence: The cache acceptance ('claims one rubbing in 6 s at a cache's dock', and 'a player holding every type in the cache can't') may end up testing a source collection instead. The HUD may show one target while the server fills the other. In `theft-loop`, a player at a mixed island who holds E past about 6 s collects both types, which breaks 'each collects a different type'. Write down the priority (for example, cache before source, then type order) and release E as soon as the first collection is done.

concerns.message: 'Wins the duel with held attack keys' is ambiguous. Duel buttons trigger on the press only (`pressed = bits & ~fighter.held`, duel/step.ts:243), and Playwright's `keyboard.down` does not auto-repeat. A key held down the whole time lands one attack.
concerns.consequence: Read literally, the host lands one jab and wins only on the 60 s timeout, plus overtime if health is equal. That adds 60–70 s to both `sea-duel` and `theft-loop`, and a draw on equal health would make the scenario fail. Define 'held' as repeated cycles of key down, at least 2–3 frames held, key up. That also fixes why the review asked for it: a `press()` can fall between two 4 ms client ticks.

concerns.message: Running integration files in parallel on a shared machine puts timing-sensitive tests side by side. The netcode harness asserts correction bounds, `inputDelay > 3` and at least 175 hash checks. Each headless duel client ticks every 4 ms. The 6 s channels need an unbroken hold: `hold()` resends every 100 ms against a 15-frame hold window (INPUT_HOLD_FRAMES), and a missed tick resets the channel (`progressChannel` requires exactly `lastTick + 1`). The per-test `testTimeout` is 20 s, while the new flows run longer. The repeated-win test alone needs about 15 s of respawn wait, 20 s of respawn protection and two duels of about 11 s each, so 60–70 s. A 60 s expiry test at production values also takes 60 s or more.
concerns.consequence: The integration check may be green for the worker and flaky under the verifier's load, or it may pass the budget only by chance. Assert timings in world ticks from events, not wall clock; this matters for the both-not-ready cancel at 10 s. Use test-only rule overrides where the test is not about the timing: `createLedger` already takes `rules`, for example a short seat reservation. Raise per-test timeouts on purpose.

concerns.message: The match game is a single Phaser game created with `Phaser.AUTO` (seaScene.ts:367-368), and it holds both the sea and the arena. The rule 'Use the canvas renderer for the arena' therefore means switching the whole match game to CANVAS, since one game cannot use two renderers. There are no WebGL-only calls (no tint, pipelines or FX), so the switch is safe.
concerns.consequence: A worker might try a second canvas-mode game for the arena, which breaks 'one Phaser game per page' and the `canvas` count of 1 that sea-duel asserts. Or the sea might quietly change renderer. Say that the whole match game becomes CANVAS, and measure frame time at sea too.

concerns.message: Protection is not ended by collecting. Today the room passes `protectionEndedBy: null` (MatchRoom.ts:335), and the plan never says to pass "collection" when a collection or cache claim starts. §2 and §6 require collecting to end spawn, win and respawn protection.
concerns.consequence: A winner or a respawned player can collect while still protected and cannot be grappled while doing it. Players could use this as a safe collection window.

concerns.message: The e2e setup uses fixed ports 2593 and 5393 with `reuseExistingServer: false` (playwright.config.ts:5-6,35,42). The machine is shared by concurrent runs, and the browser check now runs for up to 1500 s.
concerns.consequence: Another run's Playwright, if one is started meanwhile, fails to bind, and the browser check fails for reasons outside the code. This is not new, but the longer window makes a collision more likely.

simpler_alternative: Let the world tick drive every §12 timer. In `advance()`, keep a disconnect record per player: `disconnectPlayer` at the drop, a duel forfeit at 10 absent seconds counted in ticks, and `expireReservation` when the tick reaches the ledger's `reservationDeadline`. Every other non-consented leave maps to `quitPlayer`. Colyseus' `allowReconnection` is then only a longer outer bound that decides nothing. For the integration budget, use test-only rule overrides first (`createLedger({ rules })`, a short seat reservation and the encounter timings) and assert in ticks. Add fork parallelism only after the harness tests stay green under it. Seed or pin the source assignment through a test-only server setting, so every scenario can pick its island by type.
cheap_experiment: Run the current suite twice, about 10 minutes in all. First `npx vitest run --project integration --reporter=verbose` as it is now, noting each file's duration and the total. Then the same with `fileParallelism: true` in the integration project, run three times in a row. If seaDuelHarness and duelHarness keep their correction bounds, `inputDelay > 3` and at least 175 hash checks in all three parallel runs, and the longest file sets the total, then parallel forks are safe and the 60 s expiry test can run at production values. If any harness assertion wavers, go with test-only timing constants and keep files running in series.
